WhiteBIT Coin (WBT) Hits New All-Time High Above $86

📈 WhiteBIT Coin (WBT), the native coin of the WhiteBIT exchange, has reached a new all-time high of about $86. That is 18% above its previous record of $73 in August and more than 50 times its 2022 debut price of $1.62. WBT's market capitalization stands at $10.3 billion, with $180 million traded over the past 24 hours.

🌊 The move comes as the wider market climbs. Total crypto market capitalization is around $2.9 trillion, and Bitcoin is trading near $85,000 after closing last week above its 50-week moving average for the first time in 45 weeks.

⚙️ WBT is the coin that powers the WhiteBIT ecosystem, and holding it comes with practical benefits. Users who hold and stake WBT on the exchange get lower trading fees (up to 100% off maker fees, the fees charged on limit orders, depending on the holding level), free daily withdrawals of ETH and ERC-20 tokens, staking rewards, higher referral rewards and access to Launchpad, where new projects offer their tokens to users. WBT is also the native coin of Whitechain, WhiteBIT's blockchain, where it is used to pay for transactions.

🏛 WBT has also gained recognition from traditional finance. In 2025 it was added to five S&P Dow Jones Indices cryptocurrency benchmarks, including the S&P Cryptocurrency Broad Digital Market Index, institutional-grade indices that track the performance of the digital asset market.

🔥 WBT's supply is shrinking. WhiteBIT regularly burns WBT, which means coins are permanently removed from circulation and destroyed. The burns are funded by 33% of the exchange's trading-fee income and 5% of its income from other activities. The full supply was unlocked in 2026, so no new coins will be released, and the total supply has already fallen from 400 million to about 293.5 million WBT. The burns continue until 200 million remain.
